items.title: Inside Chariot: Parth Sarthi on Building Native Speech-Reasoning AI for India
items.summary:
While global frontier labs chase multi-trillion-parameter text models requiring gigawatt data centers, Indian AI startup Chariot is betting on an efficient 8-billion-parameter architecture natively engineered for speech reasoning. Co-founded by Suvrat Bhooshan (Gan.ai) and Parth Sarthi (ex-Stanford, DeepMind, Contextual AI), Chariot was selected under the India AI Mission to build sovereign voice AI. Rather than chaining together separate ASR, text LLM, and TTS models, Chariot's end-to-end speech-native architecture reasons directly in audio, eliminating translation latency and preserving pitch, emphasis, and emotional context across Indic dialects.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Parth Sarthi, Co-Founder of Chariot, to explore the future of speech-native foundation models. They discuss building beyond 22 official Indic languages into regional dialects, overcoming cross-lingual modality gaps, navigating India AI Mission GPU allocations, evaluating tokens per watt in inference workloads, and proving that surgical, domain-focused architectures can outcompete generalized text APIs.

Can end-to-end speech-reasoning models unlock the next generation of voice-first AI across the Global South?

items.title: FIRST LOOK: GalaxEye Is First Indian Startup With US Imaging Patent
items.summary:
GalaxEye has become the first Indian startup to secure a US patent for its OptoSAR imaging system, changing satellite capabilities.

This technology integrates optical cameras and radar sensors onto a single satellite, allowing for high-resolution earth observation that can penetrate vegetation and operate under diverse environmental conditions. By achieving this patent, the company sets a new benchmark for satellite imaging in the Indian deep-tech space.

This development highlights the growing sophistication of domestic space tech, proving that specialized hardware like the OptoSAR system can compete on a global stage. The ability to fuse these sensing modalities creates significant advantages for monitoring resources and infrastructure from orbit.

items.title: REPORT: RBI Warns Banks as AI Speed Raises 3 System Risks

This analysis breaks down the three primary threats, speed, concentration, and opacity, that regulators are monitoring within the financial sector AI landscape. We examine why these developments matter for future fintech regulations and how they will shape the oversight of algorithmic finance in the coming years.

items.title: Math Is Hostile Ground For A Language Model
items.summary: In episode 1025 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Luis Serrano, Founder of Serrano Academy about why talking is probabilistically easy for a language model but math is not. He explains that a model throws a dart into the vicinity of the answer: close enough works in text, but in math one millimetre off turns two plus two into 4.1. Math, and code, are hostile spaces where a right answer is surrounded by wrong ones.

The facility will scale production capacity to 2.5 lakh units annually as the Bengaluru-based EV maker targets volume expansion into mass-market electric two-wheelers and scooters. items.title: INSIDE: IDFC FIRST Sarvam Plan Self Improving Bank Lab
items.summary:
IDFC First Bank is partnering with Sarvam AI to build the world's first self-improving bank. Here is what that means for finance.

IDFC First Bank and Sarvam AI are establishing a joint R&D lab to rethink financial operations. This initiative focuses on developing systems that learn directly from customer interactions and decision-making patterns, aiming to create a self-improving bank that adapts in real-time to user needs.

For stakeholders in the fintech sector, this move signals a shift toward more autonomous, intelligence-driven infrastructure. By integrating advanced banking AI, the collaboration seeks to push the boundaries of how institutions process data and deliver services, moving beyond traditional automation toward adaptive, evolving models.

Apple has officially started its journey in the foldable market with the launch of the iPhone Duo. This passport-style device features a precision carbon fiber hinge, housing a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer cover.
